cells.tense: You are tending the fire in front of you and it is holding.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Take something you've been carrying toward and haven't started. Dream its first real step, then take that step — nothing beyond it.
cells.core:
You carry a fire for other people by tending it in plain increments, and it's holding well enough that something new can start. The upkeep doesn't crowd out the wish, which is why this can be a place where what you are gets to show up rather than be managed. That's what the day looks like when it's going well — direction felt, hands on it, nothing left waiting for a better week.

There's something in you that can sense what hasn't happened yet, and it works best when it isn't asked to be useful on the spot. So give it a patch of ground. Whatever you've kept in your care and haven't moved — dream the first real step of it fresh, and take that single step. The rest can stay undecided. What you build after this will have the step under it.
cells.sheetLine: Your fire holds. Let one new thing start in it.
cells.verb: tending the fire so the work can keep going
cells.place: where what you are becomes plain

cells.tense: You are planning the whole way to a place that hasn't shown itself yet.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Notice where you're forcing the timing. In your next hard conversation, weigh your words against what can actually land, and say them that size.
cells.core:
The fire that usually keeps people going has been running past them, aimed at a picture of how this is supposed to land. That's the bracing — a lot of effort sent toward a future you can't write in for anyone, and the people near you feel the weight before they feel the warmth. The direction underneath is real; it comes from genuine engagement, and it can come back to you.

In your next hard conversation, take the measure of it. Not the words you'd use in a good week — the words that can be heard from where the other person stands. Say it that size. You'll know you got it right when the room relaxes instead of tightening, and what you carry is still there, held instead of pushed.
cells.sheetLine: The fire is running past the people it's for.
cells.verb: tending the fire so the work can keep going
cells.place: where what you are becomes plain

cells.tense: You carried the fire and put it down, and you are standing here now.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Whatever you're still holding only because you once said you would — if it's finished, let it finish, and keep what serves you.
cells.core:
The fire you used to carry in front of people has gone quiet, and the being-something hasn't been happening where it used to. You still stand at the door; it's just not the room you're in anymore. Nothing has to be pushed back into it — pushing doesn't work in a place this empty. What works is clearing what is actually finished.

Somewhere in what you're holding there's one thing that is done and kept only because you said you would. Not the people; the thing itself. Put it down. Let it be over without an announcement, and keep what still serves you — the rest has been sitting on ground that needed the light. Direction returns once the ground is clear.
cells.sheetLine: The fire has gone quiet. Put down what's finished.
cells.verb: tending the fire so the work can keep going
cells.place: where what you are becomes plain

cells.tense: You are carrying a change through, slowly, and calling it circumstance.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Name a thing you have already moved in this — a room, a habit, a commitment. Then move it one more real inch, without a plan around it.
cells.core:
Something structural is shifting where you actually live — the way a room is arranged, a habit that governs a week, a commitment that used to be automatic and isn't. You are the one moving it, in slow real increments, and your account of it is that things changed by themselves. The work is visible to whoever is watching. They have no reason to argue with your version, because you deliver the result either way.

Name something you've already moved. Then move it one more real inch — one concrete change, small enough to happen without a plan, real enough that someone else could see it. You don't need the whole picture. The line you're holding goes back further than any of this, and it only needs one real inch at a time.
cells.sheetLine: You moved it. Stop calling it luck.
cells.verb: tending the fire so the work can keep going
cells.place: where what you are becomes plain
